summary: This is a clean, additive extension of the already-working domain-scoped ChatGPT/Z.AI manual-bridge audit to module-scoped requests: it adds one new library (scripts/module_gap_audit_lib.py) and a generator script, and extends generate_chatgpt_audit_request.py / ingest_chatgpt_audit_response.py with a mutually-exclusive --module/--repo mode that leaves the existing --domain mode's code paths untouched. It reuses the existing schema, write-scope guard (guarded_write), and versioning/allocation logic without modification, matching the standing instructions' preference for extending rather than forking mechanisms. Subprocess calls use list-form args (no shell=True), so there is no command-injection risk despite --module/--repo being user-supplied CLI input, and the module/repo linkage checks in ingest are correctly non-fatal warnings mirroring the existing files_analysed-on-disk check pattern. I independently verified the diff's claims rather than trusting the self-report: the 5 real request files exist on disk under /opt/veridian/chatgpt-audit/_pending_requests/ matching the sizes/names claimed, the MODULE_GAP_AUDIT_MODULE_LIST_2026-07-25.yaml's per-repo chunk/module totals sum correctly to the grand total of 1195 quoted in MASTER_INDEX.yaml, and a live re-run of the discovery logic for the erp_cash_management module reproduced the exact file list, line count, and byte count recorded in that YAML. No .sql/migration/schema files, auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths, or .env files are touched by this diff, and no .github/workflows/** files are touched, so the tier1 classification and the hard workflow-file rule are both correctly inapplicable here. The task is honestly scoped (explicitly states 184/189 modules and 1190/1195 request files remain, with no claim of full coverage), and there is no scope collision with other in-flight work in MASTER_INDEX.
